The Chemistry & Biochemistry Department emphasizes a polytechnic, “learn-by-doing” approach, where students engage in extensive laboratory study using advanced instrumentation-such as FT‑NMR, GC‑MS, LC‑MS, X‑ray diffractometers, and confocal microscopes. With three undergraduate subplans-American Chemical Society, Biochemistry, and a flexible General option-and a master’s program grounded in thesis research, students build a robust foundation for diverse careers. Faculty members not only teach, but also model the teacher‑scholar ethos through active research, frequently collaborating with local industries and winning grants (e.g., CSUBIOTECH awards). Students benefit from rich experiential learning: undergraduate research, co-op placements, and senior thesis projects spanning one to two years. The department hosts SMACS (Student Members of ACS) for professional development, and students can secure paid research positions via grants or earn course credit through internships. courses.title: Chemistry in Our World
courses.description: [GE 5A] Analysis of important concepts, principles and applications of chemistry for non-science-majors. Topics include atomic theory, organic and biochemistry with application to foods, drugs, medicines, fossil fuels and energy production, polymers, plastics and fibers. This course is not intended for science majors. This course is not open to students who have credit in CHM 1210.

courses.title: Chemistry in Our World Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Exploration of chemistry concepts, principles, and applications through experiments.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1010 or concurrent enrollment.

courses.title: General Chemistry for Engineers
courses.description: Provides engineering students with a background in pertinent concepts and principles of chemistry. Topics include atomic theory of structure and bonding, stoichiometry, gases, equilibrium, oxidation-reduction, electrochemistry, thermodynamics, and reaction kinetics, and their applications to engineering.
courses.prerequisites: C or better MAT 105, MAT 106, MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 120, MAT 125, MAT 130, MAT 191, MAT 214, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, STA 1200 , SAT Math>=550, or ACT Math>=23.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry I Activity
courses.description: Optional recitation to accompany CHM 1210 and CHM 1210L including group tutorial activities in General Chemistry. Students may take the lecture course without taking the recitation but may not take the recitation without the lecture and/or laboratory course. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 . Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: [GE 5A] Continuation of the development of fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including kinetics; equilibria, including acid-base chemistry; buffers; titrations; thermodynamics; electrochemistry; colligative properties; and nuclear chemistry. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: General Chemistry II Activity
courses.description: Optional recitation to accompany CHM 1220 and CHM 1220L including group tutorial activities in General Chemistry. Students may take the lecture course without taking the recitation but may not take the recitation without the lecture and/or laboratory course. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220 . Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 1220L .

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1220. Qualitative analysis. Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry
courses.description: The fundamental concepts of organic chemistry will be presented, for students who are required to take one semester of organic chemistry. Topics covered include chemical bonding, molecular structure, stereochemistry, nomenclature, physical properties, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, organic reaction mechanisms, synthesis and biomolecules. Not open to chemistry majors. Not open to chemistry majors.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to general techniques of the organic laboratory for the separation, purification and identification of organic substances. Survey of simple reactions of various functional groups. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L ; or concurrent enrollment in CHM 2010 .

courses.title: Environmental and Social Justice through Chemistry
courses.description: Investigate environmental and social justice issues in chemistry as they relate to struggle, resistance, racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation, as experienced and enacted by Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans and/or Latina and Latino Americans. Fundamental chemistry concepts such as acid/base chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry (structure, bonding), analytical chemistry, electrochemistry, radiochemistry, aerosol chemistry, and green chemistry will be discussed as implicated in past, present, and future structural issues and policies. Government entities that set policies and standards for workplace and environment, and enforce compliance will also be discussed (OSHA, EPA, AQMD, NRC).
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
courses.description: Fundamentals of gravimetric and volumetric analysis. Acid-base concepts and pH calculations. Statistical concepts including data reduction and error analysis. Introduction to modern instrumental analysis. Focus on laboratory work, with class discussion supplying supporting theory. Corequisite(s): CHM 2210L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamentals of gravimetric and volumetric analysis. Acid-base concepts and pH calculations. Statistical concepts including data reduction and error analysis. Introduction to modern instrumental analysis. Focus on laboratory work, with class discussion supplying supporting theory. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 2210 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 , and C- or better in CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Introduction to Organic Molecular Modeling
courses.description: Conformational analysis of molecules and visualization of their properties. Illustration of structure determinations, energies, and related background principles.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 314, CHM 2010 or CHM 3140 .

courses.title: Chemical Communication Activity
courses.description: This course covers the fundamentals of accessing, interpreting, and communicating chemical information.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1220 or CHM 123, and C- or better in CHM 1220L or CHM 123L.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students Activity
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students Laboratory
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Modeling the Fundamentals of Physical Chemistry
courses.description: [GE 5D] Examine models of thermodynamic properties of chemical species and mixtures, chemical kinetics, physical properties of molecules. Not a substitute for CHM 3040, CHM 3050, CHM 3110, or CHM 3120. Not a substitute for CHM 3040, CHM 3050, CHM 3110, or CHM 3120.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Elements of Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Part of a yearlong course in physical chemistry covering the properties of gases, chemical thermodynamics, solutions, physical and chemical equilibrium, electrochemistry, and macromolecules. Does not have to be taken in sequence.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Elements of Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: Part of a yearlong course in physical chemistry covering quantum mechanics, reaction kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and spectroscopy. Does not have to be taken in sequence.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Classical Physical Chemistry
courses.description: Physical chemistry covering the properties of gases, chemical thermodynamics, solutions, physical and chemical equilibrium, electrochemistry and kinetics. Required for certification by the American Chemical Society. Part of a two-semester sequence.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Quantum Physical Chemistry
courses.description: Physical chemistry covering quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, advanced reaction kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and spectroscopy. Required for certification by the American Chemical Society. Part of a two-semester sequence.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; PHY 133L or PHY 1520L ; and MAT 216, MAT 224 or MAT 2250 can be concurrent.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Modern concepts of chemical bonding, molecular structure, conformations, nomenclature, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, stereochemistry, organic reaction intermediates and mechanisms, and synthesis. The physical properties, preparations and reactions of alkanes, haloalkanes, alkenes, alkynes and alcohols.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and C- or better in CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Introduction to synthesis, isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds. A focus of this applied learning will be the theory, interpretation, and application of identifying compounds utilizing IR and NMR spectra. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140 or CHM 315; CHM 3140 can be concurrent.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: The study of the properties, synthesis and reactions of alcohols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, enols and enolates, carboxylic acids, carboxylic acid derivatives, conjugated systems, aromatic compounds, amines. Special topics include advanced synthetic strategies, biomolecules, and polymers.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140 , CHM 315, or CHM 315B.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: The principles of synthesis, characterization isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds. A focus of this applied learning will be the theory, interpretation, and application of identifying compounds utilizing IR, NMR, Mass Spectroscopy. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140L or CHM 318L; and CHM 316 or CHM 3150 . Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 3150 .

courses.title: Elements of Biochemistry
courses.description: Introductory course in biochemistry that surveys the major topics of the discipline; including the structure and functional properties of the biomolecules, and the principles of catabolic metabolism.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1220 or CHM 122; and C- or better in CHM 315, CHM 201, CHM 2010 , or CHM 3150 .

courses.title: Biochemistry I
courses.description: Biochemistry that systematically covers the topics of biomolecule structure and function. The first semester course of a yearlong course. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): CHM 3270LW .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1220 , CHM 1220L , CHM 3150 , and CHM 3140L ; D or better in BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Biochemistry II
courses.description: Biochemistry that focuses on the topics of anabolic and catabolic metabolism, the regulation of metabolism, enzyme mechanisms, and cofactors. The second semester course of a yearlong course.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3270W , and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3270LW .

courses.title: Biochemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Experimental biochemistry that systematically covers protein purification, biomolecular assays, thermodynamics, and bioinformatics. The second semester course of a yearlong course.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3270W , and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3270LW .

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to the principles and procedures used in the clinical laboratory for the analysis of blood and urine specimens. Corequisite(s): CHM 3310L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 321, CHM 3210 , CHM 3280 , or CHM 328 and CHM 329; CHM 321L, CHM 328L and CHM 329L, or CHM 3280L ; CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to clinical laboratory processes and techniques, with an emphasis on quality control processes and critical evaluation of data. Corequisite(s): CHM 3310 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 328 and CHM 329, or CHM 3280 ; CHM 328L and CHM 329L or CHM 3280L ; CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: The Chemist in Industry
courses.description: Survey of the roles and the expectations for chemists in industry and the applications of chemical reactions and principles, including consideration of economics and patents.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 201, CHM 2010 , CHM 314 or CHM 3140 ; CHM 1220 or CHM 123; and CHM 1220L or CHM 123L.

courses.title: Spectroscopic Methods
courses.description: Theory and practice of modern analytical techniques based primarily on atomic and molecular spectroscopy. Corequisite(s): CHM 3420L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221, CHM 2210 or CHM 221B; and C- or better in CHM 221L, CHM 2210L or CHM 221LB.

courses.title: Spectroscopic Methods Laboratory
courses.description: Hands on experience with a variety of modern analytical techniques based primarily on atomic and molecular spectroscopy. Corequisite(s): CHM 3420 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM221, CHM 2210 , or CHM221B; and CHM221L, CHM 2210L , or CHM221LB.

courses.title: Separation Methods
courses.description: Theory and practice of modern analytical separation methods primarily encompassing various chromatographic techniques. Corequisite(s): CHM 3430L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221, CHM 2210 , or CHM 221B; and C- or better in CHM 221L, CHM 2210L , or CHM 221LB.

courses.title: Separation Methods Laboratory
courses.description: Hands on experience with modern analytical separation methods primarily encompassing various chromatographic techniques. Corequisite(s): CHM 3430 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221, CHM 2210 , or CHM 221B; and C- or better in CHM 221L, CHM 2210L , or CHM 221LB.

courses.title: Electroanalytical Methods
courses.description: Theory and practice of modern analytical electrochemistry, with particular emphasis on potentiometry, voltammetry, amperometry, coulometry, chronopotentiometry and cyclic and pulse methods. Corequisite(s): CHM 3440L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221B or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221LB or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Electroanalytical Methods Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience with electrochemical methods used in quantitative analysis. Emphasis is placed on potentiometric titration, ion selective electrodes, coulometry, conductometry, cyclic voltammetry and polarography. Corequisite(s): CHM 3440 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221B or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221LB or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Theory of Chemical Instrumentation
courses.description: Analytical chemists are required to setup, troubleshoot, repair and sometimes construct the instruments they use for analytical measurements. Designed to explain the theory and application of some commonly used electronic components and techniques in modern instruments, such as microcontroller, AD/DA conversion and data acquisition, sources of noise in instrumental analysis, circuit of noise filter and signal amplification. Corequisite(s): CHM 3470L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 344 or CHM 3440 ; C- or better in CHM 344L or CHM 3440L ; C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and C- or better in PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Theory of Chemical Instrumentation Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience with the application of some commonly used electronic components and techniques in modern instruments, such as microcontroller, AD/DA conversion and data acquisition, sources of noise in instrumental analysis, circuit of noise filter and signal amplification. Corequisite(s): CHM 3470 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 344 or CHM 3440 ; C- or better in CHM 344L or CHM 3440L ; C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and C- or better in PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory experiments illustrating principles of physical chemistry such as thermodynamics, spectroscopy, chemical kinetics and biophysics.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 305, CHM 3040 , CHM 3050 , CHM 312, CHM 3110 or CHM 3120 .

courses.title: Introduction to Molecular Simulations
courses.description: Modeling of electrostatic interactions between atoms and molecules.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 2600 ; and CHM 3120 or CHM 3050 .

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, including group theory; solid-state chemistry; orbitals; bonding theory; molecular structure; electronic structure and spectra; main group and transition metal chemistry; acid/base and redox chemistry; coordination chemistry; thermodynamics; kinetics and mechanisms; organometallics; and catalysis. Required for certification by the American Chemical Society.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 ; or CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 ; or CHM 313 or CHM 305.

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Types of polymers and polymerization reactions; properties of polymer solutions and the determination of molecular weights; elasticity and other bulk properties.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Reaction Kinetics
courses.description: Kinetics and mechanisms of chemical reactions including transition state theory, collision theory, photochemical excitation and dissociation, solvation effects, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , or CHM 3050 .

courses.title: Introduction to Colloid and Surface Chemistry
courses.description: Examination of gas-liquid, gas-solid, solid-liquid interfaces, as well as adsorption and surface area determination, the electrical double layer and its relation to colloidal stability, and electro-kinetic phenomena.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 305, CHM 313, CHM 3040 or CHM 3110 .

courses.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
courses.description: Advanced treatment of chemical thermodynamics, and the relationship between chemical potential, molecular structure, and statistical mechanics
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , or CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , or CHM 313 or CHM 305.

courses.title: Macromolecular Modeling
courses.description: Theoretical studies and applications of computational techniques to macromolecular (e.g., polymers, proteins, and nucleic acids) structure, stability and function.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 2600 ; and CHM 327, CHM 3270W , CHM 321 or CHM 3210 .

courses.title: Computational Biochemistry
courses.description: Computational methods in modern biochemistry including sequence entry and editing, sequence alignment, phylogenetic analysis, homology searching, elementary protein structure prediction, and evaluation of 3-D molecular structures
courses.prerequisites: CHM 2600 ; and CHM 327, CHM 3270W , CHM 321, CHM 3210 or BIO 4300 .

courses.title: Methods for Data Acquisition and Analysis
courses.description: Theoretical concepts required for the collection and analysis of data, along with experimental considerations for implementation of particle/electron/photon counting for quantitative analysis are explored.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , CHM 313 or CHM 305 and CHM 352L or CHM 3520L .

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced treatment of quantum chemistry emphasizing approximation methods
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3050 , CHM 3120 , CHM 305 or CHM 313.

courses.title: Computational Chemistry
courses.description: Applied quantum mechanical studies of molecular geometries; electronic excited states, potential energy surfaces, and conformational structures are explored

courses.title: Solution Equilibria in Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Study of advanced acid-base theory, complexation, nonaqueous acid-base, solvent extraction and ion-exchange equilibria
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Organic Synthesis
courses.description: An advanced theoretical and practical study of modern methodologies and strategies in synthetic organic chemistry.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 , C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L , D or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 , and D or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Organic Synthesis Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced laboratory course focusing on multistep organic syntheses. Utilization of modern techniques to synthesize, purify and characterize organic compounds. Corequisite(s): CHM 4220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 , C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L , D or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 , and D or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects. Corequisite(s): CHM 4230 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Organic Analysis
courses.description: Advanced treatment of modern methods for the structural determination of organic compounds. Emphasis will be on spectroscopic methods, but classical functional group analysis will also be explored. Spectroscopic methods include IR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, advanced NMR experiments (e.g., DEPT, HETCOR, COSY, HMBC, NOESY), and mass spectrometry.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Organic Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Purification and structure determination of organic compounds using modern techniques and spectroscopic methods as well as classical functional group analysis. Projects include natural product isolation and separation and identification of mixtures of unknowns. Corequisite(s): CHM 4240 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Internship in Chemistry
courses.description: On-the-job training and work experience in the chemistry field under the guidance of a faculty internship coordinator and on-site job supervisor. The internship is arranged by the student and may not be a continuation of an ongoing job or volunteer experience. A minimum of 4 hours per week (60 hours/semester) per unit credit. Grade will be based on a written evaluation from the job supervisor and an evaluation of the student presentation and/or written report by the internship coordinator. Student must be enrolled in CHM 4410 during the term in which work at the internship site is done. Hours worked in one term may not carry over into another. A maximum of 4 units of CHM 4410 may be allowed as elective units for each option in chemistry (ACS approved, biochemistry or general). May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of 60 units, Overall GPA 2.0 or higher and Signed application.

courses.title: Modern Mass Spectrometry and FT-NMR
courses.description: Introduction of the theoretical and practical applications of one- and two-dimensional NMR and mass spectrometry, including instrumentation and spectral interpretation. Gain basic understanding of a variety of NMR pulse sequences and have a fundamental and technical understanding of ionization sources, mass analyzers, and their limitations.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 342 or CHM 3420 ; C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Environmental Analysis
courses.description: Sample collection and preparation techniques for different environmental media, such as water, air, and soil. Instrumental analysis of various environmental samples. Corequisite(s): CHM 4490L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2210 and CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Environmental Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Instrumental analysis of various environmental samples collected from different environmental media, such as water, air, and soil. Corequisite(s): CHM 4490 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2210 and CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Bioanalytical Chemistry
courses.description: Analytical techniques used in the study of problems in biotechnology and clinical medicine. Uniqueness of problems inherent to the analysis of biological samples, contemporary methodologies and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 327 or CHM 3270W ; C- or better in CHM 327L or CHM 3270LW ; C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Bioanalytical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Application of state-of-the-art separation and assay techniques to problems in biotechnology and clinical medicine. Corequisite(s): CHM 4500 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 327 or CHM 3270W ; C- or better in CHM 327L or CHM 3270LW ; C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Enzymology
courses.description: Detailed examination of the structure, function, kinetics, inhibition, and regulation of enzymes. Corequisite(s): CHM 4510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Enzymology Laboratory
courses.description: Experimental aspects of advanced enzyme kinetics and inhibition. Corequisite(s): CHM 4510 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Advanced Biomolecular Structure
courses.description: Examines the relationships between the structure and function of the major biomolecules.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Informational Biomolecules and Recombinant DNA
courses.description: Mechanisms of information transfer in biochemistry including the molecular details of DNA replication, DNA recombination, DNA repair, RNA transcription, protein synthesis, and recombinant techniques.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Advanced Metabolism
courses.description: Detailed examination of advanced metabolic pathways, mechanisms, and regulation.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Analytical Toxicology
courses.description: Sampling from Living subjects and postmortem; sample treatment; fundamental theory of commonly used analytical methods, such as colorimetry, fluorimetry, atomic absorption spectrometry, mass spectrometry, chromatography and immunoassay; the analysis of different type of toxicants, such as toxic gas, volatile hydrocarbons and halogenated compounds, inorganic anions, metal ions, pesticide, food additives, drugs and doping in sports. The enrollment is typically limited to 32 students.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2210 / CHM 2210L , CHM 3150 , and CHM 3140 .

courses.title: Green Chemistry
courses.description: Principles and important concepts of green chemistry. Exploration of how organic chemistry, product development, plant safety, market development, environmental impacts, and financial incentives holistically affect the development of green processes and cleaner technologies.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Air Pollution Problems
courses.description: Concepts of air pollution: major air pollutants; sources; future problems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L ; and CHM 305, CHM 313, CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , or CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 .

courses.title: Senior Project I
courses.description: The 1st semester of a yearlong course that focuses on mentor-guided and hands-on independent research or projects.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2910A and Instructor Consent.

courses.title: Senior Project II
courses.description: The 2nd semester of a yearlong course that focuses on mentor-guided and hands-on independent research or projects.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 4610 and Instructor consent.

courses.title: Research Student Seminar
courses.description: Capstone course that focuses on preparation and presentation of the thesis/project work from CHM 4610 & 4620.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 4610 and Instructor consent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced treatment of quantum mechanics and quantum field theory of chemical problems including variation, perturbation, and computational methods.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Chemical Spectroscopy and Characterization
courses.description: Application of electronic, vibrational (IR/Raman), rotational, and nuclear spectroscopies, scattering methods and atomic force microscopy to characterization of matter
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Chemical Kinetics
courses.description: Kinetics and mechanisms of chemical reactions including transition state theory, collision theory, photochemical excitation and dissociation, solvation effects, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Synthetic Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Study of main group and transition group organic reactions with focus on reagents, mechanisms, stereochemistry and retro-synthetic analysis as applied to multi-step synthesis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Current Advances in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Recent advances in topics in a select area of organic chemistry are examined: for example, reaction mechanisms, spectroscopy, heterocycles, natural products, organometallic, bioorganic, industrial and photochemistry. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Communication
courses.description: Fundamental and advanced techniques used for accessing, interpreting, and communicating chemical information. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Applications of advanced instrumental analysis to explore problems associated with analytical, organic, inorganic, physical and biochemistry.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Equilibria and Kinetics
courses.description: Advanced chemical equilibria including acid-base concepts, pH, and application to physical and physical organic chemistry.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry
courses.description: Examination of advanced and selected topics in biochemistry with topics ranging from protein conjugation, post-translation modification of proteins, nucleic acid metabolism, the omics (e.g. , proteomics, genomics, glycomics, and lipidomics), bioinorganic chemistry, bioorganic chemistry, advanced membrane dynamics, photosynthesis, anaerobic metabolic pathways, biosynthesis, signaling, and neurotransmitter biochemistry. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, which will build on concepts introduced in CHM 4010, including bonding, reactivity and spectroscopy in physical inorganic and organometallic chemistry, with a focus on applying theory to current research.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Current Advances in Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, which may include organometallic chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry, computational chemistry, spectroscopy, solid-state chemistry, or f-element chemistry, with a focus on current chemical literature. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Instrumental Analysis
courses.description: Theory and application of instrumental analysis in contemporary areas such as pharmaceutical chemistry, environmental chemistry, food chemistry and clinical chemistry from the perspective of an analytical chemist.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Water Sampling and Analysis
courses.description: Chemical principles that govern the reactions, transport, effects, and fates of chemical species in water, including sampling techniques and analytical methods.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.description: Research in area of specialization conducted as part of the preparation for writing a thesis under the direction of a faculty member. Total credit limited to 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.title: Master’s Thesis
courses.description: Compilation, evaluation, interpretation and report of research for thesis. Completion of approved, bound thesis. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
